title: House votes to block Obama's immigration actions, revealing new GOP divisions
text: House Republicans voted on Wednesday to roll back years of President Obama's immigration policies, mounting a new attack on his executive actions as part of a plan to renew funding for the Department of Homeland Security. In doing so, however, Republicans revealed fresh splits in their enlarged ranks, as more than two dozen members, mostly from suburban districts in swing states, voted against plans to end a program that grants temporary legal status to hundreds of thousands of “dreamers” — children brought into the country illegally by their parents, who have been the emotional centerpiece of the years-long debate. House passage of the spending bill is only the opening act in a debate expected to run into late February, when homeland security funding expires. Legal challenges to Obama's immigration orders, led by Republican state attorneys general, are already underway. A senior GOP lawmaker suggested on Wednesday that House and Senate leaders might also go to court. The bill passed 236 to 191, with the support of two moderate Democrats, but 10 Republicans voted against the final bill. Earlier, 26 Republicans — among them several new members from suburban districts around Chicago, Las Vegas, Miami and Philadelphia — joined Democrats in voting against a proposal to end Obama's Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program. Rep. Mario Diaz-Balart (R-Fla.), a veteran Miami Republican who voted against both the bill and the DACA amendment, said his party would not be able to settle the immigration fight until it reaches a bipartisan compromise with Obama. “Regardless of what happens this week, this month, on this issue, it will not make the issue itself go away,” he said. But Rep. Robert Aderholt (R-Ala.) said he was encouraged by the strong support the bill received from fellow Republicans.

title: Mural Of Gov. LePage In KKK Garb Throws Maine City Into Uproar
text: Portland, Maine has been plunged into pandemonium after a mural appeared showing the state's bigoted governor dressed up in full Ku Klux Klan regalia. The original graffiti art was painted on the wall of the Portland Water District's wastewater treatment plant and showed Maine Gov. Paul LePage wearing the trademark hood and robe of the KKK. Considering the stream of racist remarks he spews almost nonstop, the image is pretty fitting. Beside the 6-foot-high likeness of LePage are the words racist, homophobe and moron. Governor, the last word on the list, is crossed out with a red line. Talking Points Memo tweeted on September 6, 2016: "City won't remove graffiti of 'racist' Maine Gov. LePage wearing KKK hood" The wall art set off a string of graffiti, and the image has gone through several transformations since. Portland resident Mark Reilly painted over the image with white paint, then a group of women scrubbed off his cover-up. By 10pm on Tuesday, the image had been cut down to just LePage's face with Mickey Mouse ears above his head. Every reference to the KKK was gone, and the mural now reads only No Hate and Hate is Hate. City officials, meanwhile, have been in turmoil over what to do about the graffiti. Portland Mayor Ethan Strimling wanted the image taken down. "I do not want it up there. It is not reflective of our values," Strimling said Tuesday. "The KKK has a long, problematic history in the state of Maine, and equating the governor and his rhetoric, as much as we disagree with it, is a step too far." The wall belongs to the Portland Water District, which has not removed graffiti from it in decades, and it has been treated as a public canvas.

title: New York City Schools Drop Kellogg's Cereals for a Healthier Breakfast Option
text: The New York City public school system has stopped serving a Kellogg's brand cereal to students and replaced it with a healthier, organic cereal made by a small California company. Last year the Kellogg Company discontinued several flavors of its Kashi brand cereal, which was marketed as a healthier cereal option. Rather than simply choosing other Kellogg's brands to replace Kashi, school officials decided to hold taste tests of other, newer brands. In the end the district picked the Back to the Roots brand, The New York Times reported. According to the paper, the new brand has lower levels of sugar and salt and fewer calories than any of the Kellogg's cereals. The small company's product also contains no preservatives and has no artificially added vitamins. Its cereals are also certified organic. “Breakfast is really important to us, and we're trying to get our menu to where we want it to be,” Eric Goldstein, the chief executive of the Office of School Support Services, told the paper. “In the world we live in, though, there are so many constraints, so being able to offer Back to the Roots cereals for us is like a breath of fresh air.” Up to 254,000 children a day eat breakfast at New York City schools, according to district officials. The decision to replace several Kellogg's brands with the healthier option follows pressure from Congress, the state and some parents for schools to make better choices in their school food programs. New York school officials also said that in the taste tests, children chose the Back to the Roots brand over the others.

title: Venezuela: Maduro Says Opposition Is 'Murdering Their Own Protesters'
text: Venezuela's socialist dictator Nicolás Maduro said on national television on Saturday that the country's opposition was “murdering its own protesters,” naming people killed by Venezuelan soldiers and Chavista gangs and accusing the opposition leadership of staging the deaths to win support for its cause. Maduro offered no evidence to back up his claim. “These protests today are only in one percent of the nation,” Maduro said on state television. “They are more violent than ever, you have all seen cases where they have murdered their own protesters.” He listed three cases of alleged staged murders: two people shot dead and a third allegedly electrocuted. “If it weren't for Julio Borges and the MUD none of these tragedies would have happened,” he alleged. Borges is president of the National Assembly, the federal legislature, and a party leader in the coalition known as the Democratic Unity Roundtable (MUD). He has himself been a victim of state violence, beaten by a Chavista gang (colectivo) near the entrance to the National Assembly building in 2016. The gang managed to break his nose. In a separate video segment, Maduro also personally blamed Borges for allegedly sending a gang to kidnap a bus driver. Maduro did not say who kidnapped the driver or why, but by Monday Venezuelan state television was featuring a photo opportunity of Maduro with the driver, identified as Leonardo Leconte, on its online front page. At least 39 people have been killed in the latest wave of protests, which started in March after the Supreme Court attempted to nullify the National Assembly and make itself the main lawmaking body.
